title: Seasonal variation of soil respiration in restored upland peatlands

headings.text: Seasonal variation of soil respiration in restored upland peatlands

key_sentences: Peatland restoration by ditch blocking is widely used to raise water tables and reduce carbon losses, but its effect on soil respiration over the seasons is poorly known.
We measured soil CO₂ efflux monthly for two years at three restored and three unrestored sites on a blanket bog in the northern uplands.
Mean annual efflux was 31% lower at restored sites, and the difference was largest in late summer when water tables at unrestored sites fell below 25 cm.
Northern peatlands store about one third of global soil carbon while covering only a small fraction of the land surface.
In this study we ask whether restoration reduces soil respiration evenly through the year or mainly in the warm and dry months.
The study was carried out on a blanket bog at 420 to 510 m above sea level with a mean annual rainfall of 1,840 mm.
Soil respiration followed a clear seasonal cycle at all sites, with the lowest values in January and the highest in August.
Our results show that the benefit of ditch blocking is concentrated in the warmest and driest part of the year.
Ditch blocking reduced soil respiration by almost one third, mainly by preventing deep summer drawdown of the water table.
